decisions.issues: Small problems only. The silver chain of office hangs in a long loop down his back, so it looks worn back to front. The smoke is a row of several small plumes rather than one thin line, but it still reads as a distant line on the horizon. The sentry also has a topknot and moustache, but his mundu and crossed belts keep him distinct from Nagoji. Nagoji matches his sheet and the ch26 row: topknot, grey at the temples, curled moustache, clean chin, small gold ear stud, white coat over a red waistcoat with brass buttons, breeches and boots. There is no text in the art, and the open sky on the upper right takes both captions easily.

Nagoji's left coat sleeve is rolled to mid-forearm, which contradicts the closed cuffs in 1.1. On the bare forearm the brand is painted as a crisp dark emblem, a star or cross-like glyph, plus a scar, and it sits on the outer forearm. The bible requires a pale puckered patch blurred past reading, never a symbol and never on the outer forearm. The script does not call for the brand here at all. The sentry also changes from 1.1: he now wears a white turban and a full beard, where in 1.1 he was bare-headed with a topknot and a clean chin. A second guard has also been added. The two separate smoke columns and Nagoji's face are good.
decisions.correction: Keep this composition: Nagoji straightened at the laterite parapet in the white European-cut coat, red waistcoat and silver chain, one hand on the stone, and two separate grey smoke columns far apart on the horizon. Both coat sleeves stay down to the wrists with the same white turned-back cuffs as in panel 1.1. Show no bare forearm, and no brand, scar, tattoo, mark or symbol of any kind on his arms or hands. The sentry must be the same man as in panel 1.1, and he is the only guard. He is bare-headed with long black hair in a topknot, with no turban and no head cloth, a thick moustache and a clean-shaven chin with no beard. He wears a white mundu with crossed leather belts and now stands straight with his spear held upright, no longer leaning. Nagoji keeps the grey at his temples, the small gold ear stud and a clean-shaven chin and jaw with no stubble.

decisions.issues: Small problems only. Ramayyan still faces Padmini with his stylus and has his back to the doorway, so only three of the four heads turn to the runner. Varma's hair knot sits at the back of his crown rather than above his left ear. Nagoji's ear stud reads pale rather than gold. Ramayyan shows a faint moustache that is not on his sheet. Otherwise the whole cast is present and on model: Padmini with grey in her coiled hair, gold, sari and stick; Ramayyan with receding hair, white cloth, stylus and palm leaves; Varma bare-headed and bare-chested in gold necklaces on the platform, spear beside him; Nagoji by a pillar in coat, red waistcoat and chain. The sweat-slick runner bursts through the main doorway. The cloth map has ink lines and no lettering. The lamps are brass with open wicks. Lettering placement: the caption can sit over the roof tiles at top centre, and the runner's balloon over the door lintel at top right.

This panel is a photoreal 3D render with heavy depth of field, which clashes with the inked comic style of 1.1 to 1.3. The runner does not match 1.3: he has a topknot, a beard, a shoulder cloth over his chest, a cross strap and two satchels, where 1.3 shows short curly hair, a clean chin and a bare chest. The hall has also changed: plaster walls, slit windows and a side doorway. Varma's dais and seat are visible and empty, which breaks continuity. The stick has a polished brass ferrule and seems to touch the floor, unlike Padmini's rough natural staff held an inch above it.
decisions.correction: Render in the same inked comic line art with flat painted colour as panels 1.1 to 1.3: clean black outlines, no photographic or 3D-render look, no heavy depth-of-field blur except the soft foreground stick. The runner must be the same man as in panel 1.3. He has short curly black hair with no topknot, a thin moustache and a clean-shaven chin. He is bare-chested and slick with sweat, with no shoulder cloth, strap or satchel, and wears only a short plain white cloth tucked at the waist. He is barefoot, down on one knee, panting, with one palm flat on the floor. Use the same war hall as in 1.3: dark carved wooden pillars, warm interior light and brass standing lamps with open flames, with the sunlit open main doorway he ran through behind him. Frame low and tight on the runner so the map table, the dais and Varma's seat are out of frame, with no empty throne and no other figure. In the soft-focus left foreground show only the bottom of Padmini's walking stick, rough unpolished dark-brown natural wood as on her sheet with no brass ferrule. Hold it clearly an inch above the floor, with a visible gap and its small shadow below. Leave plain floor or dark wall at the top of the frame for two balloons.

decisions.issues: The foreground runner has red smears on his upper arm that read as blood, which breaks the no-blood rule. He also wears a head cloth and a coarse tunic, where in 1.3 he is bare-chested. Nagoji has lost the grey at his temples that he shows in 1.1 to 1.3 and that the ch25-27 row requires, and his ear stud reads silver. Varma now has grey temples and a topknot on his crown instead of black hair in a side knot above his left ear, which makes him look like the older Nagoji. Extra attendants and guards appear that were not in 1.3. The script beat is missed: this is a medium group shot with every man sharp, not a close-up on Padmini with the men soft and blurred.
decisions.correction: Frame close on Padmini from the chest up, filling the left and centre of a wide frame. She turns slowly toward the runner off-panel to the right, calm and level-eyed, with grey through her black hair coiled at the nape, simple gold, a cream sari with a gold border and her walking stick. Render the men behind her soft and out of focus, but keep them on model. Nagoji has clear grey streaks at the temples as in panels 1.1 to 1.3, a small gold ear stud, a curled moustache and a clean-shaven chin. Ramayyan has receding hair and plain white cloth. Varma has black hair with no grey in a side knot above his left ear, no topknot on the crown, is bare-chested and wears gold necklaces. Add no extra attendants or guards. Leave the runner off-panel. If any part of him shows at the right edge, he is bare-chested and sweat-slick with short curly black hair, no head cloth or tunic, and clean skin with no red marks, cuts or wounds. Keep a band of plain, dim hall wall across the upper part of the frame, clear of faces, for two balloons.

decisions.issues: Minor: Varma's dais is visible and empty in the centre background. In 1.3 he sits on it, and in 2.4 he leans forward on his platform, so it reads as if he has stood up. Otherwise clean. Ramayyan matches his sheet (receding hair, curly black sides, thin fine features, plain white cloth). The beat is exact: he pinches the bridge of his nose, palm leaves are spread and the stylus is laid down. The map is ink lines and dots with no lettering. Hands are sound. There is ample lettering space on the plain upper wall (x 0.40-0.80, y 0.02-0.33) and over the lower-right map area.

Clean. It is a figureless high-angle view: pepper vines on rough posts on both sides of a narrow path, a canal with low cargo boats, and two small shrines half swallowed by foliage on the ridge. Two smoke trails rise, one from the northern hills and one from the coast. No figures (the boats are empty), no lettering and no anachronism. The lettering can sit in the sky band at the top and on the low-detail distant plain and sea at upper right. Varma is speaking off-panel from the hall, so his tail goes to the top edge.

The brand on Nagoji's bared left forearm is drawn as a crisp dark glyph that looks like an '&' or an '8' with a tail. It reads as a legible tattooed symbol, which is pseudo-text and breaks the bible rule (a pale blurred burn, no legible letters or numerals). It sits right beside the key action, the pointing finger, so the letterer cannot cover it. Secondary problems: light stubble dots on his chin and jaw, and an empty royal throne in the centre background, although Varma is on his platform in 2.4. Everything else works: both likenesses (topknot with grey temples, thick curled moustache, gold ear stud, white coat, red waistcoat, silver chain, breeches and boots; Ramayyan with stylus and palm leaves), the finger on an unlettered ink map, and the hall setting.
decisions.correction: Keep this composition, camera angle, lighting and both likenesses exactly as they are: Nagoji leaning over the table at left with one finger on the cloth map where the path narrows, Ramayyan seated across the table at right holding a stylus and a palm-leaf bundle, and the map drawn in ink lines only with no lettering. Change only these points. Nagoji's white coat sleeves stay buttoned down to the wrist on both arms, so no skin of the forearm shows: no brand, no scar, and no glyph, symbol, letter, numeral or tattoo-like mark anywhere on him. His chin and jaw are smooth and clean-shaven with no stubble dots. Turn the background toward carved pillars and a plain shadowed wall so the royal dais and throne are out of frame. Keep the band above both heads as low-detail wall or shadowed roof so two speech balloons can sit there without touching either face.

decisions.issues: Varma does not match his sheet or the chapter row. His hair is in a crown topknot with a gold band, the same arrangement as Nagoji's, instead of the side knot above his left ear seen in 1.3. His face is younger and broader, with the same heavy curled moustache as Nagoji, so the two men read as near twins in the same panel. The V13 Varma has a leaner, older face and a finer upturned moustache. Nagoji's bared left forearm also shows a red, cross-like brand blotch, which breaks the 'not a cross' rule, and his jaw has light stubble. The background guards wear white turbans and red sashes instead of the Travancore white mundu with crossed leather belts. The composition, the hall and Nagoji's downward, troubled look at the map all work.
decisions.correction: Keep this composition, hall, lighting and Nagoji's pose exactly: Nagoji in the left foreground leaning over the unlettered ink map with his eyes on it and a troubled frown, and Marthanda Varma behind at right, standing on his raised platform and leaning forward with both hands on its edge. Redraw Varma strictly from the V13 varma-v1 sheet: his lean, older face with sharp cheekbones and a finer moustache with upturned tips, clearly a different man from Nagoji. He is bare-headed with his long black hair tied in a side knot above his LEFT ear, exactly as in page 1 panel 3. No crown topknot and no hair band. Keep him bare-chested in a cream mundu with a gold border, with gold necklaces and his spear beside him. Nagoji's white coat sleeves stay buttoned to the wrist on both arms so no forearm marks show, and his chin is smooth and clean-shaven. Any background guards wear white mundu with crossed leather belts, with no turbans and no red sashes. Keep the upper band of roof shadow and plain wall between and above the two heads low-detail for two speech balloons.

decisions.issues: The framing misses the script. 2.5 asks for a tight shot on Nagoji, lit from the side, with the smoke seen through a window slit behind him. This is a medium-wide room shot: his head fills only about 40 percent of the height, the light is flat daylight and the smoke shows through a large opening off to the right. Two background guards wear rust-red turbans with broad red sashes. That is Nagoji's old commander look, not the Travancore white mundu with crossed belts, and it does not match the white-turbaned guards in 2.4. Varma's red daybed sits empty with his spear, although he is present in 2.4. Nagoji himself is right: topknot with grey temples, thick curled moustache, gold ear stud, coat, waistcoat and chain, the fist-to-mouth brooding expression, and only light stubble.
decisions.correction: Recompose as a true close-up in this wide strip. Nagoji's head and shoulders fill most of the panel height and sit in the left-centre third, three-quarter view facing frame right, eyes lowered, his fist pressed against his lips. Keep exactly the troubled expression, likeness and costume of the current image: Kerala topknot, grey at the temples, thick curled moustache, clean-shaven chin, small gold ear stud, white European-cut coat, red waistcoat, brass buttons and silver chain of office. His coat sleeves stay buttoned to the wrist so no forearm marks show. Light him with a hard raking side light from a narrow vertical window slit just behind his shoulder at frame right, leaving the far side of his face in shadow. Through that slit, two faint grey smudges of smoke on the distant horizon. Fill the rest of the frame with plain shadowed stone wall, low in detail, so a caption at upper left and a short speech balloon near his mouth can sit without touching his face or hand. No guards, no other figures, no throne or daybed, and no text.

decisions.issues: Minor only: the kneeling runner named in the art direction is not in frame (the hall-gone-still beat is still clear: Padmini's head snapped to Nagoji, Ramayyan and Varma frozen, guards at the doors). Varma's hair is a crown knot rather than the bible's side knot above the left ear, but this matches 1.3 and 2.4. Nagoji's breeches read as long trousers tucked into tall boots. Ramayyan's stylus rests on the leaf instead of hovering above it. Nagoji's face, stud, clean chin, uniform and the white scar on his left forearm are correct. The map is ink and wash only, with no lettering. Caption can sit top left over the roof beams and doorway; Padmini's small balloon fits on the dark wall between her head and Varma.

v01 (only candidate): the brand on Nagoji's inner left forearm, which sits at the centre of the panel as he leans on it, is drawn as a dark-outlined crescent or eye-shaped tattoo symbol, not the bible's pale puckered patch. The map has several tiny letter-like scribbles (pseudo-labels) right beside his pointing finger and among the hills. The background is crowded with extras who double Nagoji: a guard in a rust-red turban, cream tunic and broad red sash (his old commander look), and two men with his topknot, curled moustache and gold ear stud. There is also a man in an ochre tunic with an indigo sash who reads as a raider. A cushioned dais with a spear beside it stands empty behind him, though Varma sits there in 3.1 and 4.1. A leather belt with a brass buckle is strapped over his waistcoat. Face, topknot, grey temples, clean chin, stud and the pointing gesture are good.
decisions.correction: Keep the composition and pose: Nagoji alone in focus, leaning over the map table in the same war hall, right index finger tracing a thin zig zag along the canal, left palm flat on the cloth map. Keep him as drawn: Kerala topknot, grey at the temples, thick curled moustache, clean-shaven chin, small gold ear stud, white European-cut coat hanging open over a red waistcoat with brass buttons, silver chain of office, knee breeches, no belt or buckle over the waistcoat. His inner LEFT forearm shows only a pale, puckered patch of raised scar tissue, lighter than his skin, with no dark outline or ink. It has no crescent, eye, spiral, symbol or tattoo shape. Beside it runs one long thin white scar from wrist toward elbow, and there are no other marks on his arms. The cloth map is ink lines only (canal, dotted path, ridges, tiny tree marks), with no letters, words, numerals, labels or letter-like squiggles anywhere, especially near his finger. Background: only two or three Nair guards at the doorways in white mundu, white head cloth and a crossed leather belt. Do not draw anyone in a red turban or broad red sash, anyone in ochre or indigo, or any other man with a topknot, curled moustache and gold ear stud. Either keep Varma's dais out of frame, or show Varma seated on it (bare-chested, gold necklaces, spear beside him). Leave the plain upper wall to the right of his head clear for two balloons.

decisions.issues: v01 (only candidate): Nagoji's inner left forearm, clearly visible on the chair back at frame right, carries a dark ink tattoo of a spiral-over-circle glyph that reads as a script letter or symbol. This breaks the no-pseudo-text rule and the bible's brand description (pale puckered patch, no letters, no symbol). Everything else works: the two-shot across the map table, Padmini with her stick, grey threading and cream gold-bordered sari with the old drape, Nagoji turning to face her with a correct face, stud, clean chin and uniform, the same hall and lamps as 3.1, a map with no lettering, a plain red banner, and clear wall between the pillars for three balloons.
decisions.correction: Keep everything that works in this frame: the two-shot across the map table in the same war hall, Padmini at left standing with her long stick (grey threading through black hair coiled at the nape, cream sari with a gold border in the old Kerala drape with no blouse, gold earrings and necklace) glaring at Nagoji, and Nagoji at right straightening from the table to face her (Kerala topknot, grey at the temples, thick curled moustache, clean-shaven chin, small gold ear stud, white European-cut coat, red waistcoat, brass buttons, silver chain of office, breeches and boots). Keep the plain wall between the pillars clear for balloons. Fix one thing: Nagoji has NO tattoo and no dark ink, spiral, circle, glyph, letter or symbol anywhere on his skin. The old brand on his inner LEFT forearm is only a pale, puckered patch of raised scar tissue, lighter than his skin and without any outline, beside one long thin white scar from wrist toward elbow. It is acceptable to turn that forearm so the inner side faces away, or let the coat sleeve cover it. The red banner stays plain cloth with no device or writing.

decisions.issues: Minor only: in the soft background at right, a dais with a cushion and a spear beside it is empty, a small continuity slip against Varma being present in 3.1 and 4.1. A tiny pen-like scribble on the curled corner of the background map (about 20 px, near x 0.85, y 0.95) could be cleaned in retouch. Otherwise it matches the beat: tight on her large, anatomically sound fist clenched on the head of the stick, her face above it, eyes fixed on Nagoji off-panel right. She has grey threading, gold earrings, necklace and bangle, and the cream gold-bordered sari with no blouse. Both balloons fit on the rafters and wall at upper left, or on the plain wall at right between the window slits.

Varma's face, side knot, mundu, necklaces and the unlettered ink-line map with fort marks are right, and the spear tip on the canal works. But the hall is suddenly full of about eight unscripted councillors sitting on the floor around a low table (white and maroon turbans, grey beards), plus extra guards. Page 3 and 4.3 show only the principals, a waist-high map table and one or two distant guards. Varma is standing on the floor at the table, not on his platform, and he is looking at a seated stranger instead of between the off-panel Nagoji and Padmini.
decisions.correction: Show Marthanda Varma alone, standing at the front edge of his low platform (the same low platform with the cushioned seat seen on page 3). The platform sits right at the far end of the waist-high wooden map table, and he leans down so his spear tip runs along the canal line of the cloth map toward the fort marks. Keep his face, black hair in the side knot, cream gold-bordered mundu, gold necklaces and the clean ink-line map exactly as drawn. Draw NO other people at or around the table: no seated councillors, no men sitting on the floor, no turbaned, maroon-turbaned, bald or bearded onlookers. At most two small Nair guards in white mundu with crossed leather belts may stand far back by the main doorway, as on page 3. His eyes glance sideways past the frame edge toward the off-panel Nagoji and Padmini. Keep the upper third (roof beams and plain back wall) clear and low in detail for two speech balloons.

decisions.issues: Padmini matches her sheet and the ch26 row (grey threading in coiled hair, simple gold, cream gold-bordered sari, stick). The beat fails, though. Varma's platform is plainly visible behind her and EMPTY, so she cannot read as turning to face the king. Instead she is looking at a row of unscripted seated men (bearded, bald, topknotted) who fill both foreground corners. None of them appear on page 3, and the low floor-level council table does not match it either.
decisions.correction: Keep Padmini exactly as drawn: face, grey-threaded coiled hair, gold, cream gold-bordered sari and walking stick. Frame her knees-up in three-quarter view, her head and shoulders turning sharply toward the right edge of the frame, where the king sits off-panel on his platform. Put the side wall, a carved pillar and a doorway behind her so the empty platform is NOT visible. Draw NO other people: no seated men, no councillors on the floor, no bald, turbaned or bearded onlookers. If the map table shows at all, it is the waist-high wooden table of page 3 with palm-leaf bundles and the unlettered ink-line map. Keep the upper area of plain wall clear and low in detail for two speech balloons.

decisions.issues: Usable. Ramayyan matches his sheet (receding hair, curly sides, plain white cloth, stylus held still over the palm-leaf bundle) and is looking up at Padmini. She matches her sheet with the grey threading. The requested lower-right inset of her closed eyes is present, with a thin painted inset border. There is no text on the map or the banners, the hall matches page 3, and there is no invented crowd. Minor points: Varma's platform behind Ramayyan is empty (a low seat with bolsters), as in 3.3 and 3.4 but not in 4.5. In the main image Padmini's eyes are open; the inset carries the closed eyes. Plain back wall in the upper centre has room for both Ramayyan balloons.

Padmini and her stick strike, with impact lines, are good. But the 'three men' she faces are three invented strangers in the foreground: a bearded man in maroon cloth, a bald man and a bearded curly-haired man seen from behind. None of them is Varma, Ramayyan or Nagoji, so the beat reads wrong. A line of extra guards also fills the background, which does not match page 3.
decisions.correction: Keep Padmini exactly as drawn: the pose, the stick coming down hard on the floor with small impact lines, her grey-threaded coiled hair, gold, cream gold-bordered sari and wet, furious eyes. Keep the wide 3:1 strip of the same hall. Remove the three seated foreground men and the row of guards: draw NO bearded, bald, turbaned or maroon-clad men anywhere. The three men she addresses (the king, Ramayyan and Nagoji) are off-panel on the camera side, so she faces toward the viewer and her glare sweeps across the foreground. At most two small Nair guards in white mundu with crossed leather belts may stand by the far doorway. The map table is the waist-high wooden table of page 3, with palm-leaf bundles and the unlettered ink-line cloth map. Keep the upper band (roof beams and dark back wall) clear and low in detail for three speech balloons, away from her face and the stick.

decisions.issues: Nagoji matches the sheet and the ch26 row: thick curled moustache, clean chin, grey temples, Kerala topknot, small gold stud, white coat, red waistcoat, brass buttons, silver chain, breeches and boots. Varma on his platform in the background is right. But the foreground is crowded with unscripted seated onlookers (white turban, maroon turban, bald topknot, bearded men). That clashes with page 3, with 4.3 and with the crowd-free corrections for 4.1, 4.2 and 4.4. His pushed-up left sleeve shows a white scar drawn as two crossing lines, an X, which goes against the bible's 'not a cross' brand. The full-figure framing also weakens the tight-throat nod.
decisions.correction: Keep Nagoji exactly as drawn: face, thick curled moustache, clean-shaven chin and jaw, grey at the temples, Kerala topknot, tiny flush gold ear stud, white European-cut coat, red waistcoat, brass buttons, silver chain of office. Frame him as a medium shot from the waist up in the same hall, head dipped in one small nod, jaw set, throat tight. Remove every seated onlooker in the foreground: no turbaned, maroon-turbaned, bald or bearded men. At most one or two standing Nair guards may stay far back by a pillar, and Varma may remain small and soft-focus on his low platform in the background, as drawn. Both coat sleeves stay down to the wrists, so no forearm scar or brand shows. Keep the upper right (roof and back wall) clear and low in detail for two speech balloons.

decisions.issues: v01 is strong on everything except Kayal. Nagoji matches the sheet and the ch26 uniform row: topknot, grey temples, clean chin, curled moustache, gold stud, white coat, red waistcoat, chain, breeches, boots and talwar. Ponnan is half a length behind on Nagoji's left with his spear, red shoulder cloth, short jacket and bare knees. The Travancore riders have crossed belts under the red conch standard, and there is smoke with sparks ahead and open sky for both captions. The problem is that Kayal, the large foreground horse, has a clear white star and a faint stripe on her forehead. The Kayal sheet and the bible say plainly that she has no white markings. Kayal shows no marking in 5.2 and 5.3, so the star would also break continuity across this page.
decisions.correction: Kayal, the bay mare Nagoji rides at the head of the column, must have NO white markings anywhere. Her face is solid ochre red-brown from forelock to muzzle, with no star, stripe, blaze or snip. She has a black mane, tail and lower legs and an ochre quilted saddle pad, exactly as on her sheet. Keep everything else in this composition unchanged: Nagoji at the head in the white European-cut coat, red waistcoat, brass buttons, knee breeches, boots, silver chain and talwar, with Kerala topknot, grey temples, clean-shaven chin, thick curled moustache and small gold ear stud; Ponnan half a length behind on his left on the smaller horse, with his spear and red shoulder cloth; the Travancore riders with crossed leather belts under the red silver-conch standard; the dry red road, the greasy smoke columns and sparks ahead, and the open sky at the top left for the two captions.

decisions.issues: Usable with minor deviations. The riders are painted in full colour instead of silhouette, only Nagoji and Ponnan are shown rather than the reined-in column, and the vantage is only slightly raised, so it reads less as looking down from a ridge. The raiders are also quite close to the riders. Everything else checks out: Nagoji matches in profile (topknot, grey, clean chin, moustache, stud, uniform, chain), Kayal is plain bay with no markings, and Ponnan is correct. The pepper rows, the bare-chested raiders in head cloths with musket smoke, the loaded boats on the canal and the small leaf-swallowed shrine all match the script. There is no painted text and no gore. The caption fits in the sky and distant-hill band across the top centre and right.

Usable with two minor gaps. Ponnan turns toward Nagoji from his own horse rather than leaning in at Nagoji's shoulder, and Nagoji is pressing on the saddle at the start of a dismount, not yet swinging down. Both characters otherwise match their sheets and the ch26 rows. Ponnan rides the smaller horse a head lower and Kayal has no markings. The shrine, the canal boats and the smoke match 5.2. There is no text and the hands are sound. Ponnan's balloon can sit over the vine tops at top left, and Nagoji's two balloons fit in the open sky and smoke at top right.

Usable. The memory faces are more solid painted portraits than the smoke-textured stain the script asks for, though they are muted, grainy and dissolve into the smoke at their lower edges. Revathi's grey threading is faint but present, and a pendant at her throat reads as the tali. Padmini is greyed, with the stick head beside her. The soldier wears a white turban, unlike the bare-headed riders in 5.1. A few distant structures burn beyond the canal, which is acceptable as the raiders' fires. Nagoji is correct on foot at an untouched green vine line, in the full uniform with clean chin and stud, and the scar is on his left forearm. Dry leaf litter is under his boots and the torch handoff hands are sound. There is no text. The caption fits in the open sky at top left.

v01 has four problems. (1) Nagoji has visible stubble and beard shadow on his chin and jaw, which breaks the clean-shaven rule; stubble is allowed only in captivity. (2) The white scar shows on the outer forearm of his near, right arm, but the bible puts it on the inner LEFT forearm. (3) The beat is not met. The script asks for a tight shot with Nagoji's face behind the torch, lit orange. Here it is a medium crouch with his face off to the left in flat daylight, not behind the torch. (4) A tall flame climbs the bark of the post and the leaf litter glows, so the fire reads as already caught. That spoils the 'nothing happened' page turn the script holds back.
decisions.correction: Reframe as a true close-up. Press the oil-soaked torch head against the dry leaves and bark at the base of one wooden vine support post. Put Nagoji's face close behind and just above the torch, lit warm orange from below by the torch flame, eyes fixed on the point of contact, waiting. The flame only touches: it is the torch's own small flame and nothing has caught yet, so no fire climbs the post, the leaf litter is not burning and no embers spread. Nagoji's chin and jaw are completely clean-shaven, with no stubble, stipple or beard shadow; he has a thick curled moustache, a small gold ear stud, a Kerala topknot and grey at the temples. The white coat sleeve stays down over the wrist of the hand holding the torch, so no scar or mark shows on that arm (his brand and scar are only on the inner LEFT forearm). Keep the daylight pepper garden with green vines and fruit, the white European-cut coat, red waistcoat, brass buttons and silver chain. Leave clear, soft background (sky or blurred vines) in the upper-left quarter for the caption.

decisions.issues: Clean. Nagoji matches the sheet and the ch25-27 row: topknot, grey at the temples, thick curled moustache, clean-shaven chin, gold ear stud, sooty white coat, red waistcoat, brass buttons, silver chain, breeches and buckled boots. He steps back from the burning post with the torch raised, and white steam shows at the stem. Shrine, canal and pepper boats match 6.2 to 6.4. One nit: a faint pale smudge about 25 px wide on the inner right wrist of the torch arm looks like faint glyph strokes when zoomed 10x. At print size (1:1) it is only a tiny smudge. Optional retouch. No lettering is needed.

Acceptable. The beat reads: a raised view of separate post fires with gaps between them, Nagoji walking the row with a torch, and Travancore men (white mundu, crossed belts) lighting post after post on either side. His face matches the sheet (stud, clean chin, moustache, topknot, grey temples). The long thin white scar is correctly on his inner LEFT forearm. Minor continuity point: his coat has no soot here, although 6.1 shows soot 'already' on it. The Travancore men wear white head cloths. Their white mundu and crossed belts still set them apart from the raiders. Caption space is the smoky sky at top centre and right (x 0.38 to 0.95, y 0 to 0.07), above the canal treeline.

Acceptable. Fire has leapt from the burning vines onto a pile of fallen branches, with black smoke boiling up. Two Travancore men (white mundu, crossed belts) flinch back from the heat with sound hands and anatomy. The canal, boats and shrine continue 6.1 and 6.2. Minor point: two boatmen in the background (one poling, one seated in a boat) look unbothered by the fire. The long caption can sit in the clear blue sky at top centre-right (x 0.45 to 0.8, y 0 to 0.18).

Acceptable. Travancore musketeers kneel in a line at the edge of the burn and fire into the smoke. They wear white mundu and crossed leather belts, with no blue or red coats. Raiders show as dark head-clothed silhouettes against the flame under a plain, unlettered faded-green banner. Minor points: the raider silhouettes look like they wear tunics rather than bare shoulders. The locks read more like flintlocks than clear matchlocks, which is not noticeable at this scale. Caption space is the smoky sky at top left and centre (x 0.17 to 0.55, y 0 to 0.12).

The only candidate has a defect I would not print. Nagoji's bare left forearm, the arm hauling the man, carries a white jagged scrawl on its OUTER, upper surface. At full size it looks like cursive handwriting, which counts as pseudo-text in the art. It also breaks the bible: the brand and scar belong only on the INNER left forearm, never the outer forearm. Everything else works: soot-streaked face, clean chin, moustache, gold stud, topknot, grey temples, sooty white coat, red waistcoat, chain, breeches and boots. He hauls a Travancore man in a crossed belt by the shoulder cloth while raiders cough and stumble in the smoke with arms over their faces. There are no bodies, and the sky at top centre has room for both captions.
decisions.correction: Keep this exact composition, setting, lighting and staging. In the foreground left, Nagoji runs toward the viewer's left: soot streaks on his face, Kerala topknot, grey at the temples, thick curled moustache, clean-shaven chin, small gold ear stud, sooty white European coat, red waistcoat with brass buttons, silver chain of office, knee breeches and buckled boots. With one hand he hauls a coughing Travancore man (white mundu, crossed leather belts) back out of the smoke by his shoulder cloth. Coughing, stumbling raider silhouettes, arms over their faces, stay in the grey smoke behind, with the shrine, canal and pepper boats at left and smoky open sky across the top. Change only his arms: both white coat sleeves come down to his wrists, sooty but NOT rolled up, so neither bare forearm shows. Paint no white lines, scribbles, scratches, scars, tattoos or marks on either forearm or the back of either hand. The old brand and long white scar sit only on the INNER left forearm and are hidden under the sleeve in this panel. Nothing resembling handwriting, letters or symbols anywhere on skin or cloth. The raiders in the smoke wear dark indigo or earth-brown cloth and head cloths, with bare shoulders.

decisions.issues: Minor: the distant survivors walk upright carrying spears and a long gun instead of limping. The wading figure's grey short-sleeved shirt, back straps and round cap look slightly modern, and the straps could be read as Travancore cross-belts. All of them are tiny at print size. Everything else is on script: a burned corridor through standing pepper, fallen charred posts, a dropped flintlock and a scorched plain green banner with an unlettered pale disc. There are no bodies and no text, and the sky across the top has clear room for both captions.

Nagoji's coat sleeves are pushed up to the elbows. His RIGHT forearm, the one holding the cup, next to his face, shows a dark ring mark like a tattoo plus a white scar, and his left forearm shows another scar. That puts a brand-like mark on the wrong arm. The bible row puts the brand and scar on the inner LEFT forearm only, and the brand is a pale puckered patch, not a dark symbol. Padmini has a white vertical forehead mark that is not on her sheet, and a dark upper-lip shadow that reads like a faint moustache. Varma's hair hangs in loose curls instead of the side knot above his left ear. Otherwise the composition is strong and on beat.
decisions.correction: Keep this exact composition, night lamplight and placement: Varma on his low platform at the far end, sooty soldiers in white mundu sitting along the walls, the map table at left, Nagoji seated in the right-centre foreground lowering a brass cup from his lips with a grimace, and Padmini entering through the side doorway at frame right with her stick. Fix the following. Nagoji's white coat sleeves are worn DOWN to the wrists with soot-blackened cuffs, so no forearm skin shows on either arm. No tattoos, circles, symbols, scars or marks anywhere on his hands or wrists; his brand and scar are on the LEFT forearm and stay hidden under the sleeve in this panel. Padmini has no forehead mark and a clean, smooth upper lip with no shadow that could read as hair. Her grey-threaded black hair is coiled at the nape and damp at the temples. Put the soot streaks on the lower half and hem of her cream sari and keep the drape over her shoulder clean. Varma is bare-headed with his hair gathered in a side knot above his LEFT ear, with no loose curls and no turban. Varma, the soldiers and Nagoji's eyes all turn toward Padmini at the door.

decisions.issues: Minor continuity points. Padmini's sari is clean here, but the arrival wide (7.2) has soot on it. The 7.2 correction moves the soot to the lower sari, which the table hides in this panel. Varma's knot sits toward the back of his head, not clearly above his left ear. His platform backdrop is dark wood rather than the red cushions of 7.2. Padmini matches her sheet: grey threading, gold beads and studs, cream sari with a gold border, stick in her right hand. She looks straight down the lens at Nagoji with a flat face, and Varma is a lamplit figure on his platform behind her. The map is ink lines only. The balloons can go top centre to right over the roof beams and wood wall, above Varma's head.

Nagoji's bare left forearm has a dark, letter-like glyph that looks like a tattoo, plus a pink scar line. That is pseudo-text in the art, and it contradicts the bible's brand: a pale puckered patch with no letters and no symbols. Varma's platform in the background is an empty seat with a red cushion, which contradicts 7.3, where Varma sits on it. The guards wear red turbans and red sashes with no cross-belts, unlike the bare-headed sooty soldiers of 7.2. The staging is also flipped: Padmini is on the left and Nagoji on the right, against 7.2's geography, where Padmini is on the right, and 7.5, where Nagoji looks toward frame right.
decisions.correction: Keep the waist-high two-shot across the map table, with the ink-line map (no lettering), palm-leaf bundles, brass lamps and warm night lamplight. Keep Padmini standing unmoving with her stick and her hard, flat stare. Keep Nagoji's open-palm answering gesture and his look: Kerala topknot, grey at the temples, thick curled moustache, clean-shaven chin, small gold ear stud, white European-cut coat, red waistcoat, brass buttons, silver chain of office. Change the following. Mirror the staging so Nagoji stands on the LEFT of the table facing right and Padmini on the RIGHT facing left. Nagoji's coat sleeves are DOWN to the wrists with soot-blackened cuffs and no bare forearm. No glyph, symbol, tattoo, letter-like mark or scar is drawn on any skin. Varma is present as a lamplit figure on his low platform in the background behind Padmini: bare-headed, hair in a side knot above his LEFT ear, bare-chested, cream mundu with a gold border, gold necklaces. The royal seat is never empty. The background soldiers match the previous wide: sooty Travancore men in white mundu with crossed leather belts, bare-headed, sitting quietly along the walls, with no turbans, no red turbans and no red sashes.

decisions.issues: Minor background inconsistencies. A seated figure who resembles Varma wears a cream upper cloth with a gold sash and loose hair, and sits at the table level instead of bare-chested on his platform; he can read as an unnamed councillor. The guards wear white turbans with red sashes, unlike 7.2's bare-headed soldiers. The coat shows no soot, but the cuffs are out of frame. Nagoji himself matches his sheet and the bible row: thick curled moustache, a clean chin with only light hatching, small gold ear stud, grey at the temple, topknot, white coat, red waistcoat and silver chain. His troubled gaze toward frame right fits 7.2's geography, with Padmini on the right. There is clear wall, window and doorway space at upper right (about x 0.59 to 0.80, y 0.03 to 0.35) for both balloons.

Minor only. Padmini matches her sheet and the ch26 row: grey through her coiled hair, cream sari with gold border, old drape, stick. The soot visibly falls from her fingers onto the canal lines. The map is plain ink with no lettering, but it is untinted, while the maps in 8.2 and 8.3 have pale blue water. Her sari shows no soot smear, which matches 7.3 and 7.4. The dim dais at the back of the hall is empty, although Varma is on his platform in 8.3. Put the balloons over the ceiling and back wall at upper right.

Acceptable reverse angle over Padmini's shoulder. Nagoji is correct: thick curled moustache, clean-shaven chin, small gold ear stud, grey at the temples, white coat, red waistcoat, brass buttons, and a silver chain whose plain shield pendant has no text. His hair is a crown knot with long curls falling, the same as page 7. One continuity flaw: the red-cushioned royal seat on the dais behind the map table is empty, although 8.3 shows Varma seated there. Letter the two Padmini balloons in the upper centre between the two heads, over the ceiling and back wall; that also covers the empty seat. Padmini's mouth is hidden, so the tail points to her turned cheek.

Clean. Varma matches his V13 face and the war-hall look: bare-headed, a hair knot at the back-left of the crown above his left ear, bare chest, cream mundu with a gold border, gold necklaces, spear beside him, seated on his platform and unreadable. Padmini is half-turned toward him with her stick in hand. Soldiers in white mundu and head cloths sit along the hall. The map has pale blue water and no lettering. Put Varma's balloon on the ceiling band above him at upper right, and Padmini's two over the ceiling and door wall at upper left and centre.

Acceptable. Padmini stands at the doorway with her bare back to the hall, in profile toward the night outside, not looking round, her hand sound on her stick. Nagoji is small in the lamplight behind her: crown knot, moustache, clean chin, gold stud, white coat, red waistcoat, chain, breeches and boots. The hall is now empty of soldiers and Varma, and the royal seat at the back is empty, which is a mild break from 8.3; it reads as her isolation. The map scribble has no lettering. Put the three balloons on the ceiling rafters and the back wall in the upper left and centre, clear of both heads.

v01 is strong otherwise: right wall walk, sunset, the burned strip on the horizon, Nagoji alone at the parapet in the correct uniform (clean chin, curled moustache, gold stud, topknot, grey temples), Revathi walking toward him, and open sky for both lettering lines. It fails the ch20-28 bible row for Revathi: her hair is solid black with no grey threading. Panels 9.2 and 9.3 on the same page show a clear grey streak at her temple, so this panel would break continuity on the page.
decisions.correction: Keep this exact composition, the laterite wall walk, the tiled tower and the guards beside it, the sunset light, the dark burned strip on the horizon, Nagoji's pose leaning on the parapet and both costumes unchanged. Fix only Revathi's hair. Under the chapter 20-28 continuity she now has grey threading through her black hair, drawn as in the neighbouring panels: a clearly visible silver-grey streak sweeping back from the temple above her visible ear into the braid, plus a few fine grey strands through the black at the crown. Her face stays the age on her sheet (a little younger than Nagoji), not elderly. Keep the jasmine in her braid, the sandalwood line at the hairline, the tali on its cord, the flat-coin necklace, the gold armlets and the deep indigo sari with gold.

decisions.issues: Minor only. Nagoji is walking beside her and glancing at her rather than turning at the parapet, but the panel still reads as him turning to her while she keeps walking. Revathi has a thin red line in her hair parting that is not on her sheet or in 9.3. Both principals otherwise match: Nagoji has a clean chin, curled moustache, gold stud, topknot, grey temples and the uniform with chain; Revathi has grey threading, jasmine braid, sandalwood line, tali, coin necklace and armlets. Open sky at top centre and top right for both balloons.

Minor. The background guards wear white head cloths, while in 9.1 and 9.2 they are bare-headed. Revathi stands at Nagoji's frame-left here, while 9.2 and 9.5 put her at frame-right. Faint smoke still rises from the strip a few days later, which reads as smouldering. The beat is correct: both lean on the parapet staring at the blackened strip and neither looks at the other. Hands are sound. Both match their sheets and bible rows. Wide open sky at the top for her two balloons.

v01 fails on three points. (1) His left coat sleeve is pushed back to show a bare forearm with a white CROSS-shaped mark on the outer forearm. The bible forbids the brand from reading as a cross, puts it on the inner forearm, and the script never calls for it here; the cuff also no longer matches his other sleeve. (2) He gazes into the distance with a fist on his hip, so he is not turned toward Revathi's profile at close range, and the swaggering pose does not fit the quiet question. (3) It is framed as a wide full-figure shot rather than a small panel.
decisions.correction: Keep the laterite fort wall walk and parapet, the same sunset light and sky, the burned strip on the horizon, and Nagoji's face, Kerala topknot, grey temples, clean-shaven chin, thick curled moustache, small gold ear stud, white European-cut coat, red waistcoat, brass buttons and silver chain of office. Fix the arms: both coat sleeves stay fully down to the wrists, with matching turned-back cuffs and brass buttons on each arm. Show no bare forearm, and no scar, cross, mark or brand anywhere on his arms or hands. Frame it tighter for a small panel, chest up. His head and shoulders turn toward frame right, and his gaze is level and sideways at close range on someone standing just beside him off-panel at frame right (Revathi, who stands to his right in 9.5), not out at the distant horizon. His expression is quiet and questioning, brows slightly drawn, lips just parted. One hand rests relaxed on the parapet; no fist on the hip. Leave clear open sky above and in front of his face for one balloon.

decisions.issues: The staging of v01 is right: full-width, Revathi at the parapet facing the horizon with the last light on her face, Nagoji at the left edge watching her, the correct uniform, hands sound, and broad open sky to the right for three balloons. It fails the ch20-28 bible row for Revathi: in this large, prominent view her hair is solid black with no grey threading. Panels 9.2 and 9.3 show a clear grey streak at her temple, so the change would be obvious on the page.
decisions.correction: Keep this exact composition, the wide letterbox framing, the laterite parapet, the tower and the guards, the sunset with the last light falling on Revathi's face, her pose with both hands on the parapet, and Nagoji at the left edge in uniform watching her, all unchanged. Fix only Revathi's hair. Under the chapter 20-28 continuity she now has grey threading through her black hair, matching panels 9.2 and 9.3 on this page: a clearly visible silver-grey streak sweeping back from the temple above her visible ear into the braid, plus a few fine grey strands through the black at the crown. Her face stays the age on her sheet (a little younger than Nagoji), not elderly. Keep the jasmine braid, sandalwood line, tali, flat-coin necklace, gold armlets and the deep indigo sari with gold.

decisions.issues: v01 (the only candidate) breaks Revathi's ch20-28 bible row: her hair is solid black with no grey threading, although she has visible grey at the temple in 9.2, 9.3, 10.3 and 10.4. She also has a small nose stud that is not on her sheet. The rendering is wrong for this page: glossy airbrushed skin, heavy outlines, lipstick-red lips and a saturated pink sky, where the neighbouring panels use finely hatched ink and wash under a muted gold sunset. Her body faces the camera, with only her eyes cut toward the off-panel Nagoji, so she is not 'facing him fully'. Setting, guards, sari, armlets, tali and sky space for lettering are otherwise fine.
decisions.correction: Match the rendering of the neighbouring page 9 and 10 panels exactly: finely hatched ink line with soft wash colour, a muted gold-and-lavender evening sky, no saturated pink, no glossy airbrushed skin, no lipstick. Revathi Bayi must show clear grey threading at her temple and through the front of her hair, the same as in the other panels of this scene. No nose stud or nose ring. Keep the tali visible on its dark cord below the flat-coin necklace, the jasmine braid, the gold armlets and the deep indigo sari with gold. She has just straightened up from the laterite parapet and turns her whole body toward frame right, toward the off-panel Nagoji, her face in three-quarter view and her eyes steady on him. Keep the laterite wall walk and parapet behind her, the tiled-roof gatehouse with two white-mundu guards in crossed belts at frame left, and the dark burned strip as a line across the green on the horizon. Leave clear open sky in the upper right, away from her face, for two speech balloons.

decisions.issues: Minor only. Revathi's grey threading is subtle: grey strands in the hair sheen, not a distinct streak. The pale marks on Nagoji's bared left forearm (the scar and brand) cross slightly and, under close inspection, could read as a small cross; they match the same marks in 9.4. Otherwise clean: Nagoji has his topknot, grey temples, thick curled moustache, clean chin, gold ear stud and the full ch26 uniform with chain; Revathi wears her tali; the burned strip is a dark band in the distance; the setting matches page 9; sky space is open above both figures.

Minor. Revathi's tali is hidden by her turned shoulder. A thin gold band ties Nagoji's topknot. Revathi walks to frame right here but to frame left in 10.5. The reverse angle in 10.4 bridges the flip, but it is a small screen-direction break. The beat is right (she answers over her shoulder while walking, Nagoji stays at the parapet). Both likenesses and costumes are on model, hands are sound, and there is open sky across the top for both balloons.

v01 (the only candidate) gets the beat and Revathi right: she is a few paces off, turned back halfway in the last light, hand at the tali, with grey threading. Nagoji's foreground back view, which fills nearly half the frame, has front-of-coat features on its back. His coat is split open down the back, showing a wedge of red waistcoat with brass buttons, and the chain of office hangs in a V on his back with its medallion between the shoulder blades. It reads as a coat worn back to front, or a torso facing camera under a head turned away, and it breaks the ch25-27 uniform row.
decisions.correction: Nagoji is seen from behind at frame left, over his right shoulder. Draw the BACK of his white European-cut coat, closed and plain, with a centre back seam, back pleats and only the two hip buttons at the waist. No red waistcoat may show anywhere on his back above the waist, and there are no buttons running up the back. The silver chain of office passes over both shoulders and dips in a shallow loop across the upper back, with NO medallion or pendant on his back (the medallion hangs at his chest, out of view). Keep his Kerala topknot with grey at the temple, the small gold ear stud, the edge of his thick curled moustache in lost profile and his clean-shaven jaw. Keep everything else as it is: Revathi a few paces off along the wall walk at right, turned back halfway, her face in the last light, right hand at the tali, grey threading, jasmine braid and gold armlet; the laterite parapet, the tiled-roof gatehouse with guards at right, the sunset sky, and the burned strip with faint smoke on the horizon. Leave open sky across the top centre for two balloons.

decisions.issues: Minor. Nagoji is mid-sized in the frame rather than 'small'. Revathi walks to frame left, back toward the gatehouse she came from in 9.1, which is a screen-direction flip after 10.3 and 10.4. Otherwise it delivers the beat: she walks away along the wall walk, back straight and already small; Nagoji is alone at the parapet under a reddening sky. Both are on model (topknot, grey, moustache, clean chin, ear stud, coat with chain, breeches, boots; jasmine braid, armlets, indigo sari). No text, sound hands, and the same fort and gatehouse as the rest of the scene.

The scar is on the wrong side. Ibrahim stands at frame left with his body to camera and his head turned toward viewer's right, so the ear and cheek nearest the camera (viewer's left of his face) are his RIGHT ones. The scar runs from that RIGHT ear to the jaw, and it is painted reddish instead of the thin pale line the prompt asks for. The script needs his anatomical LEFT side with the LEFT-ear-to-jaw scar clearly visible. Everything else is good: dusk canal, moored boat, roped cloth bales, white turban, grey-flecked beard, teal short coat over a cream vest with bulging pockets, sound hands, a shadowed man seen from behind, and clear dusk sky for the captions. A horizontal mirror of v01 would put the scar on the correct side, since the frame has no text.
decisions.correction: In the last attempt Ibrahim stood at frame left turned toward viewer's right, which showed his RIGHT ear and RIGHT jaw, and the scar landed on the wrong cheek in red. Mirror the staging. The shadowed man seen from behind stands at frame LEFT. Ibrahim stands at frame RIGHT, his body and face turned three-quarters toward viewer's LEFT as he speaks to that man, so his anatomical LEFT cheek, LEFT ear and the left side of his jaw face the camera. His scar is one thin PALE line, lighter than his skin and never red, from just below the LEFT ear lobe down to the jaw line on the side of his face nearest the camera, with no mark on the right cheek. Keep everything that worked: the dusk canal with a moored boat and roped cloth bales, the clay oil lamp, his white turban, short grey-flecked beard, muted teal short coat over the cream vest with bulging pockets, white mundu and blue-striped shoulder cloth, the open-handed confiding gesture, the other man in dark cloth and shadow, and a clear band of dusk sky across the upper frame for the two captions.

decisions.issues: Minor only. Nagoji stands at the end of the table, not squarely across it. The seat on Varma's platform has a high carved back and reads a little throne-like. Ramayyan has faint grey shading on his upper lip, and both men show light stubble texture. Nagoji's left sleeve is pushed up and shows the white forearm scar. Otherwise it matches the beat: Ramayyan at his palm leaves, head down, stylus moving. Nagoji has the topknot, grey temples, curled moustache, clean chin, gold stud, white coat, red waistcoat, brass buttons, breeches, boots and silver chain. The war hall is in daylight with no text on the map or leaves, and the upper-left wall and roof are clear for the caption and Ramayyan's two balloons.

Minor. The brand on Nagoji's inner LEFT forearm, bare because both sleeves are pushed to the elbow as in 11.3, is painted as a small dark ring-shaped mark next to the white scar. Earlier bible rows describe a pale puckered patch. It has no letters, numerals or cross and is small at print size, but the author may want it checked. Nagoji has light stubble texture. Otherwise the beat is right: a two-shot at the map table, Nagoji leaning in with both hands on the table, Ramayyan writing and not looking up. The hall, uniform, chain and gold stud match 11.3, the guards wear white mundu with crossed belts, the map and leaves have no text, and the hands are sound. There is clear space top-left (doorframe and sky above the guard) for Nagoji's balloon and on the ceiling and wall above Ramayyan for his.

Wrong framing and off-model. The script calls for a tight shot of Ramayyan's hand, but this is a medium-wide shot of Ramayyan in a crowded hall. Ramayyan has a clear moustache, which contradicts his clean-shaven sheet. A bearded man in a gold-bordered mundu sits on Varma's platform and reads as an uncast king, and about seven extra courtiers and guards fill the hall. Panels 11.3 and 11.4 show it empty apart from door guards. The hands, blank leaves and peppercorn dish are fine.
decisions.correction: The last attempt drew a medium-wide shot of the whole crowded hall with Ramayyan wearing a moustache and a bearded man seated on the platform. Instead make an extreme close-up of the tabletop only, with NO faces and NO other people anywhere in the frame. Ramayyan's two thin, fine-boned brown hands enter from frame left with only the edge of his plain white cloth at the forearm. His left hand lifts and turns one blank palm leaf; his right hand holds the slender stylus, its point already pressed to the next leaf. At frame right a small brass dish of dried black peppercorns sits on top of a tied stack of finished blank palm leaves, weighing it down. The background is only a soft, dim blur of a timber pillar and laterite wall in the same midday daylight as panels 11.3 and 11.4. Keep the upper third of the strip as plain dark tabletop shadow or blurred wall for the two captions. Keep what worked: the blank palm leaves with no marks, the brass dish of black peppercorns, the warm wood table, the sound hands and the inked graphic-novel style.
